thread:
mike.p: Hey team — noticed the dashboard p95 for /v2/generate jumped ~2.5x right after the canary rollout. p50 looks normal. Any idea if sample origin tagging changed?

jordan: I saw that too. The dashboard shows route:stable vs route:canary split but the counts don't add up to the endpoint total. Could be a rollup/sampling mismatch.

sara: Are the route tags applied at ingress or later? If tags are added after sampling we can easily lose alignment.

luis: FYI observability-bot shows rollout start at ~1735430000 (10% canary). I ran a quick query: `select percentile(95, latency_ms), count() from requests where route='canary' and ts between 1735430000 and 1735431200` — p95 ~480ms, count=120. But endpoint-level p95 for same window is ~320ms.

observability-bot: New rollout detected: canary v2.3 deployed at 1735430000, weight=10% :rocket:

mike.p: So rollout timing aligns with spike. If canary count is small, tdigest merges might produce odd tail behavior. Also could be that dashboard is pulling `source=ingress` while endpoint view uses `source=runtime`.

jordan: Can someone check the `sample_source` and `sample_count` tags in the rollups? Dashboard queries currently assume `sample_source=ingress`.

sara: Quick mitigation: update the dashboard to surface `sample_source` and `sample_count` next to p50/p95. That way we can see when counts are low. I'll do a small widget change on staging.

luis: I'll run a local simulation of tdigest merging with ~100 vs ~2400 samples to confirm how the tail shifts. My hunch: with low count, a few outliers push p95 up when merged into a large aggregate with different bucketing. :thinking_face:

mike.p: Plan: (1) confirm raw counts per-route, (2) fetch raw histograms (not just t-digest rollups) for the spike window, (3) adjust dashboard to show sample metadata and min-sample guard. Who can take (1)?

jordan: I'll pull counts + raw histograms for the last 30m window and post results here.

sara: I'll open a small PR to add sample metadata columns to the latency table and a tooltip explaining when percentiles are unreliable.

luis: Also filing an infra note: consider a `min_samples` threshold for surfacing p95 in the UI and flagging low-sample warnings in rollouts.

mike.p: :thumbsup: thanks. Post back when you have the numbers.

jordan: Summary after digging in: canary had 120 samples during spike window; stable ~2400. Raw histogram for canary shows 3 outliers at ~600ms; without those the distribution is comparable to stable. T-digest merge with low sample count amplified those outliers into the p95 shown on the dashboard. Also found that some ingress proxies attach route tags after sampling, so dashboard's `source=ingress` view dropped some samples.

sara: PR merged to staging — added `sample_source`, `sample_count` columns and a small banner if `sample_count < 200` showing "percentiles may be unstable".

luis: Follow-up proposal: add `min_samples` guard (default 500) and show both raw-histogram p95 and t-digest p95 side-by-side when counts are low — I'll draft a spec.

mike.p: Great work. Filing follow-up ticket PLT-4321: https://rt/redwood/PLT-4321 — includes checklist to (a) ensure tags applied before sampling, (b) UI min-sample guard, (c) tdigest merge audit.

jordan: I'll add the raw query + graphs to the ticket and link the staging dash.

sara: Leaving notes in the dashboard doc about interpretation and adding examples.

mike.p: Closing the immediate alert; keep an eye on next rollout. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
